chapters.summary: Lincoln Restler, filling in for Chair Jim Gennaro, introduces himself and announces the committee will vote on Proposed Intro 804-A, sponsored by Councilmember Phil Wong, regarding maximum allowable illuminance of residential outdoor lighting fixtures.

utterances.speaker: Lincoln Restler
utterances.text: My name is Lincoln Ressler, and I am inadequately filling in for our distinguished chair, Jim Gennaro, who is unable to be here today.

utterances.speaker: Lincoln Restler
utterances.text: We are voting at the Committee on Environmental Protection and Waterfronts on proposed introduction 804A, sponsored by my colleague,

utterances.speaker: Lincoln Restler
utterances.text: Councilmember Phil Wong, in relation to the maximum allowable illuminance of residential outdoor lighting fixtures on one- and two-family homes.

utterances.speaker: Lincoln Restler
utterances.text: This committee first heard the bill on April 6th of this year, and I really want to commend Councilmember Wong for working so thoughtfully with colleagues to advance this final legislation.

chapters.summary: Restler explains that the bill sets a one foot-candle illuminance limit for outdoor lighting on one- and two-family homes in low-density residential areas, roughly equivalent to light from a streetlight shining into a window. He notes exemptions for construction safety lights and decorative displays like Dyker Heights.
chapters.title: Restler explains the illuminance limit and exemptions in Intro 804-A

utterances.speaker: Lincoln Restler
utterances.text: Proposed Intro 804A would set an illuminance limit of one foot candle for outdoor lighting fixtures on one- and two-family homes in low-density residential areas.

utterances.speaker: Lincoln Restler
utterances.text: For context, one foot candle is roughly the amount of light that shines into your window from a typical New York City streetlight.

utterances.speaker: Lincoln Restler
utterances.text: Certain lights, including lights for construction safety and decorative light displays, like Diker Heights, would be exempt.

utterances.speaker: Lincoln Restler
utterances.text: I think we all would agree that shining a floodlight into your neighbor's home is not very neighborly.

utterances.speaker: Lincoln Restler
utterances.text: This final legislation.

utterances.speaker: Lincoln Restler
utterances.text: Proposed Intro 804A would set an illuminance limit of one foot candle for outdoor lighting fixtures on one- and two-family homes in low-density residential areas.

utterances.speaker: Lincoln Restler
utterances.text: With that, I will pass it along to my colleague, Councilmember Wong, for some remarks on his legislation.

utterances.speaker: Lincoln Restler
utterances.text: For context, one foot candle is roughly the amount of light that shines into your window from a typical New York City streetlight.

chapters.summary: Phil Wong thanks Chair Gennaro and describes Intro 804 as a small bill with big quality-of-life impacts. He explains fixes made since the April hearing, including measuring lumens at the nearest neighbor's window, limiting the regulation to low-density districts, and adding a cure period.
chapters.title: Councilmember Wong presents his legislation and describes amendments

utterances.speaker: Phil Wong

utterances.speaker: Phil Wong
utterances.text: So the fix has now been implemented, and it provides clarity on allowable lumens

utterances.speaker: Phil Wong
utterances.text: So I thank you, everyone, and the members of this committee for moving this bill, and I hope this will get passed out of this committee.

summary: The Committee on Environmental Protection and Waterfronts, chaired by James F. Gennaro, held a hearing on September 10, 2026, to vote on Proposed Intro 804-A.
The bill, sponsored by Councilmember Phil Wong, sets a maximum illuminance limit of one foot candle for outdoor lighting fixtures on one- and two-family homes in low-density residential areas.
The committee voted 5-0 to approve the bill, with members praising the collaborative process and the quality-of-life improvements it would bring.
